scope: legacy six typed integer storage boundary only

findings.claim: The public mutation outcomes do not show which failure actually occurred. Each kill records only exit_code 101 plus an 'intended_assertion' and 'intended_kill'. Cargo also returns 101 for a compile failure. The public JSON therefore cannot tell an intended-assertion kill apart from a build or setup failure, which the requirements say earns no kill credit. The ledger's statement that every mutant reaches its assertion depends on private logs that have no published digest.
findings.evidence: Each kill check (input_tokens through repo_map_size, and ordering) has fields head/tree/path_sha256/exit_code/seconds/log/intended_assertion/intended_kill. There is no observed panic line and no log sha256. Requirements: 'compilation/setup failure or unrelated safety refusal is no kill.' Mitigation: the seven public patches are trivially compilable and deterministic. For a field-omission mutant, the earlier fields still pass the guard and the snapshot check. The omitted field then stores and panics at expect_err('overflow stored for <field>'). For the ordering mutant, the error text still matches, and the post-commit snapshot inequality panics at 'overflow published data for input_tokens'. Static tracing supports the stated kills, so this is an evidence-verifiability gap, not a causal defect.
findings.fix: For each check, record the exact observed failing assertion line (or the test-harness failure summary) and the sha256 of the retained log. Optionally record 'observed_kill' separately from 'intended_kill'. No source change is needed.

Scope reviewed: the legacy Store::put_usage signed-i64 guard, its controls and mutants, and the evidence delta 41c60fe..78676c9. No tools were used; this review relies only on the supplied public bytes. (1) Source: the guard sits at the top of put_usage, after only the read-only validate_scope. It runs before the Session lookup, the Immediate transaction, the usage INSERT and the usage.recorded audit. It covers all six u64 fields in domain::Usage. review_round is u32 and estimated_cost keeps its existing finite/nonnegative check, so no u64 field is omitted. `.into_iter().flatten().all(i64::try_from(..).is_ok())` accepts None and 0..=i64::MAX exactly, with no cast, clamp or zero-fill. Because the guard sits at the single Store write boundary, it covers every caller, so the exact caller inventory does not change its correctness. Integers inside cache_metadata (Grok cache_creation_tokens) are outside the guard, and the ledger says so explicitly. (2) Control: the state test stores i64::MAX on five fields plus a real cached zero and reads them back exactly. For each field and each of i64::MAX+1 and u64::MAX, it gets the range error. It then compares a full snapshot (Project, Goal, Task, Session with version, Task-scoped usage rows, Task-scoped audit) against the pre-state. The usage row and audit are written at usage.scope, which is the Task scope, so the snapshot observes the real write path. The fixture's worktree is a direct child of Project.worktree_root and matches the executor Session, so the prerequisites are real and are not setup failures. (3) Mutants: each field-omission patch makes the fixture reach its own `overflow stored for <field>` expect_err. The post-commit ordering patch returns the range message but leaves a committed row and audit, so it fails at `overflow published data for input_tokens`. That snapshot assertion is exactly the part the omission mutants never reach. Every patch's index line (0a023c0) matches the state/mod.rs blob in the CI provenance. The state/mod.rs and tests/state.rs path hashes are identical across control-before, control-restored and ordering-restored. The ordering-restored tree (057e999) equals the CI checkout tree and the 41c60fe tree. That makes the post-restoration control equivalent to a pre-control at the ordering baseline, and the b47b773 control has byte-identical Rust inputs. (4) Provenance: the 36 listed blobs and full_tree_equal tie CI37209367789 to the reviewed Rust bytes. The delta to 78676c9 is documentation and JSON evidence only, with no Rust or Cargo/CI input changes, so that CI still covers the current source. (5) Ledger: the corrected wording now matches what the test asserts, i.e. i64::MAX on five fields plus cached zero. Source2A is recorded as a failed, unaccepted review with sticky cleanup_unverified and acceptance false, and it is not counted as a verdict. Prior red CI results and fixture-setup failures are retained. whole_issue_acceptance is false in every artifact. Limits: I cannot externally check blob/tree OIDs, SHA-256 values, raw logs or CI job results. The main.rs, workflow.rs and context.rs bodies were not supplied, so I did not re-grep for production callers. None of this changes the guard's semantics. This approval covers only the narrow legacy integer storage boundary component. It is not acceptance of qualified telemetry, producers, epoch, native counters, benchmark or report, raw-writer retirement, #21 or MVP, all of which remain open.
